promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Skip Wednesday's tempo and get your right knee checked by a physio this week. The pain has been getting worse for four days, so running drops to two short, flat test runs until someone has examined it.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
**The knee:** I can't tell you whether it's your IT band, and a guess could point you the wrong way. Pain on the outside of the knee that turns sharp on downhills and aches on stairs needs a physio or sports medicine doctor to examine it. Book one this week. Tell them it started on a hill on Thu Aug 13 and stopped your long run on Sun Aug 16.

**Wednesday's tempo:** No, skip it. Fast running puts more load on a knee that still aches on stairs, and with ten weeks to go one missed tempo costs you almost nothing. The plan swaps it for easy cross-training. Tempo work comes back once you've had a few easy runs with no pain.

new.analysis:
**You followed the plan closely until the knee stopped you.** Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday matched the planned distances exactly. The tempo was well run: 4 mi at about 8:00/mi, even from start to finish. The long run ended at 9 of 13 mi, so the week came to 32 mi against about 36 mi planned.

**The knee got worse each time, and that is why the plan changes.** It went from 2/10 tight on Thursday's hill, to 1/10 before Saturday's run, to 4/10 and sharp on Sunday's downhills. Now it aches on stairs, which you've never had before. Once pain builds over several days and shows up in everyday life, it's time to stop training through it and get it looked at.

**This week is about protecting the knee while keeping your fitness.** Running drops to at most 7 mi, all on flat ground, with a rest day between runs and a clear rule to stop. Cross-training keeps your aerobic work going without the impact. With ten weeks to go, an easy week costs very little, but running on a knee that keeps getting worse could cost you the race.

**Keep the goal for now, because your fitness was solid before Sunday.** Your easy runs have held around 9:50/mi at 138 bpm, a touch quicker than a month ago at the same heart rate. Your tempo pace of 8:00/mi is well under the 8:35/mi you need for 3:45. We'll look at the goal again after the physio visit.

**Next week depends on how the knee handles these runs.** If both runs are pain-free and stairs feel normal, next week goes back toward your usual five days, with a flat long run of about 10 mi. If not, you stay on cross-training until a professional says you can run. If the break stays short, there is still time to build the long run toward 20 mi.

safetyCallouts.title: Get the right knee assessed this week.
safetyCallouts.body: The pain went from tight to sharp and now aches on stairs, so see a physio or sports medicine doctor before you run long or fast again.

safetyCallouts.title: Get seen sooner if it gets worse.
safetyCallouts.body: If the knee swells, gives way, or hurts more each day, stop running completely and book an appointment straight away.
